secondaryWorld.name: Kursbuch
secondaryWorld.overview:
This is a departures board for money, not a trading terminal. Everything is printed on a warm grey stock, ruled with hairlines, and read top to bottom in a single column of sections. Figures sit on a rule; they never sit in a card. The page has no shadow, no gradient, no glass, no blur, and no rounded panel: the only radius in the system is a 3px hairline nick on small inset objects. Depth is a printing problem, solved by rule weight and by two stock tints, never by lifting anything off the page.

The world deliberately refuses the terminal look that trading software defaults to. **There is no monospace anywhere in the build** — not in tables, not in chart axes, not in identifiers. Alignment of figures is bought with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums` set on `body` and reasserted on every numeric cell, which is what a timetable actually does. Typography is one family in two cuts (Archivo and Archivo Narrow) at two weights (400 and 600). The narrow cut carries every label, head, chip, tab and status line; the normal cut carries sentences and figures.

The page is built to be read by one operator at a glance, so the system spends its scarcity budget on a single reserved red. Money direction is never told in that red; it rides a desaturated tint field behind the figure instead. The whole surface is served as plain CSS and vanilla JS embedded in Python string literals — there is no build step, no framework, no icon package, and no runtime dependency beyond one Google Fonts import.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled rows on stock; no cards, no shadows, no gradients, no glass.
One reserved signal red, spent only on attention and on the live-money boundary.
Two stocks — grey newsprint for paper, rose-tinted for real money.
Archivo + Archivo Narrow, two weights, tabular lining figures everywhere.
One authored motion: a 180ms wash on a figure whose value just changed.

rules.name: The Reserved Signal Rule
rules.body: `{colors.kursbuch-signal}` means "this needs you" or "this is real money." It is spent on: the attention state of the status line, the stale rule and note, the armed/halt marks, the danger button, the notice box, the caret, the live masthead and live active-tab underline, and the LIVE cutoff marker on a chart. Adding a sixth use dilutes the other five.

rules.name: The Money-Rides-a-Field Rule
rules.body: Profit and loss direction is told by a tint field behind the figure (`{colors.kursbuch-pos}` / `{colors.kursbuch-neg}`) with the figure kept in ink — never by colouring the figure, and never by the reserved red. A losing number is not an alarm; it is a number.

rules.name: The Two Stocks Rule
rules.body: Paper trading and pipeline sit on `{colors.kursbuch-stock}`. Real money sits on `{colors.kursbuch-stock-live}` via `body.live-service`, which also swaps the masthead's bottom rule and the active tab's underline to `{colors.kursbuch-signal}`. The two surfaces must never be confusable at a glance.

rules.name: The State-Not-By-Colour Rule
rules.body: Every state that carries colour also carries a word or a shape: the stale rule goes dashed and the figures get struck through, the marks read OFF / ON / ARMED / HALT, the status line swaps a check glyph for a triangle. Remove all colour and the page still reports correctly.

rules.name: The No-Monospace Rule
rules.body: No monospace font is permitted anywhere, including chart axis labels (`11px "Archivo Narrow"`) and code-like identifiers. Numeric alignment comes from tabular lining figures, not from a fixed-pitch face. The terminal look is the rut this world was built to leave.

rules.name: The Short-Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is reserved for short labels: section heads, micro-labels, column-free field labels, chips, tabs, marks, buttons, the wordmark, and the stale mark. Anything that reads as a sentence — decks, legends, notes, empty-state copy, status-line text, notice bodies — is sentence case. The rule was tuned against the build: snake_case model names in tables are left lowercase on purpose, because upper-casing a 29-character identifier costs legibility and buys nothing.

rules.name: The Two-Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 and 600 only. There is no 300, 500 or 700 anywhere in the system; emphasis is bought with the narrow cut, letterspacing, and case instead.

rules.name: The One Dominant Answer Rule
rules.body: Each page opens with exactly one status line stating what the system is doing right now; every section below is supporting evidence. On a phone that line owns the first viewport.

rules.name: The Flush-Edge Rule
rules.body: The leftmost column of any measure grid or table drops its padding and its rule so figures align to the same vertical as the page title. Nothing is indented into a box.

rules.name: The Printed-Depth Rule
rules.body: If something needs to separate, rule it or tint it. Never lift it. A shadow, gradient, or glass panel anywhere in this world is a defect.

rules.name: The Hairline-Nick Rule
rules.body: 3px radius on inset objects, 0 everywhere else. There is no medium or large radius step, and adding one would break the printed register.

rules.name: The Drawn-Icon Rule
rules.body: Icons are inline SVG strokes at 1.6 drawn to match the type's weight, using `currentColor`. No icon font, no glyph package, no emoji.

dos: **Do** separate with a rule or a stock tint. The rule scale is 2px ink / 2px signal / 1px `rule-2` / 1px `rule`; the tint scale is `stock-sunk` → `stock` → `stock-raised`.
**Do** put every new figure block on a `.measure` grid and every new dataset in a `.sect` with a `.sect-head` and a live `.sect-note`, so its freshness is always on the page.
**Do** tell money direction with a `.fig.tint.pos` / `.fig.tint.neg` field behind an ink figure.
**Do** keep `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums` on anything numeric.
**Do** reserve uppercase for short labels and write every sentence in sentence case, including empty-state copy, notes, and legends.
**Do** give every new table a `.stack` class and `data-lab` on each `td` so it restacks into labelled rows under 640px.
**Do** pin column widths on any new table via a `colgroup` and a `.t-*` width class.
**Do** pair colour with a word or a shape for every state.
**Do** draw icons inline as 1.6-stroke SVG with `currentColor`.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion`; the global reduce block collapses all animation and transition to 0.001ms.
donts: **Don't** add a shadow, gradient, glass/backdrop-filter, or a card. Containers are sections and plates only.
**Don't** use a monospace font anywhere, for any reason, including identifiers and chart axes.
**Don't** spend `{colors.kursbuch-signal}` on anything but attention or the live-money boundary. Never on a losing number, a heading, a link, or decoration.
**Don't** colour a P&L figure itself; the field behind it carries direction.
**Don't** introduce a third font family, a third weight, or a radius other than 3px.
**Don't** uppercase a sentence, a model identifier, or anything longer than a few words.

**Don't** add a second animation. `.washed` (180ms, `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`, `{colors.kursbuch-rule-2}` fading to transparent, fired only when a figure's value actually changed) is the system's one authored moment; transitions are limited to the 160ms button colour change.
**Don't** add a build step, a framework, an icon package, or a runtime dependency. The surface is plain CSS and vanilla JS inside Python string literals.
**Don't** let the live surface and the paper surfaces converge. `body.live-service` must keep its own stock, its red head rule, and its red active tab.

narrative.overview:
Every strategy is a printed slip: numbered, staked and stamped, hanging under a live tote board. Every screen opens with a tote board, a full-width field of racetrack green (`{colors.board}`) covered in a faint lamp grid. The money figures on it are amber, set in large condensed numerals. Below the board is the counter (`{colors.counter}`), a cool grey surface. Strategies sit on it as thermal-white slips with perforated tear-off edges, a serial number (`No. 00012`), and a rubber-stamp mark that carries their state. The world rejects both the dark neon trading terminal and the white brokerage card grid. The page is a betting window, not a terminal.

Density is set for a retail trader who reads money first. Each screen has one dominant field, the board, so its figures always read first. Slips sit at registered scale in an auto-fill grid and share one sparkline axis, so you compare them by eye rather than by reading. Barlow and Barlow Condensed carry every word and number. The condensed cut, uppercase and letterspaced, is the voice of the board: figures, labels, buttons, stamps and nav. Normal Barlow is the voice of sentences: slip titles, theses, notes and chat.

The world has three pieces of authored motion. A research slip feeds down out of the board's slot as the agent prints it. A stamp then lands on it with a slight overshoot. The lamp on a LIVE plate blinks. Everything else is a short state transition, and `prefers-reduced-motion` collapses all of it.
keyCharacteristics: A green tote board owns the top band of every screen; amber figures appear only on it.
Strategies are thermal slips with perforated edges, a serial and a rotated rubber stamp.
State is a stamped word (PASSED, VOID, PAPER, LIVE), never colour alone.
Paper money and live money are told apart by a service plate on the board: an outline for PAPER, a solid amber fill with a blinking lamp for LIVE.
One family: Barlow for sentences, Barlow Condensed for figures and labels. No monospace labels.
Paper depth: one soft slip shadow on the counter; the board itself stays flat.

rules.name: The Amber-Lives-on-Green Rule
rules.body: `{colors.amber}` appears as text only on the green board or the green tab bar. On the counter and on slips, amber appears only as a solid fill (the ticket button, the live slip band, the LIVE plate). A live mark printed on white stock uses `{colors.live}`.

rules.name: The One Green Field Rule
rules.body: Each screen gets exactly one band of `{colors.board}`, at the top. The counter is never tinted green, and no second board appears further down the page.

rules.name: The Two-Widths Rule
rules.body: Labels, figures and commands are set in Condensed uppercase. Sentences are set in Barlow in sentence case. A sentence is never uppercased, and a figure is never set in the normal width.

rules.name: The No-Monospace-Labels Rule
rules.body: Tickers, serials, timestamps and chart axes are set in Barlow or Barlow Condensed, and tabular figures handle the alignment. The one place a fixed-pitch face appears is the collapsed "Exact spec" block of raw machine JSON, which is a code view rather than a label.

rules.name: The Board-First Rule
rules.body: Every authenticated screen opens with the board, and the board opens with money or the page's own measured result. The counter starts below it, and nothing comes before the board.

rules.name: The Registered-Scale Rule
rules.body: Slips in a grid share one size and one sparkline axis, so heights and lines can be compared without reading the numbers.

rules.name: The Paper-on-a-Counter Rule
rules.body: Things on the counter rest on it with the soft slip shadow. Things on the board are recessed into it. Nothing on the board floats.

rules.name: The Perforation Rule
rules.body: Only a slip, meaning a strategy, hypothesis or deployment, gets perforated edges. Panels and rows are ordinary stock with a 3px corner. If an object is not a strategy, do not tear it.

dos: **Do** open every authenticated screen with the green board and put money or the page's measured result in its lead cell.
**Do** keep amber text on green only. On white stock, mark live money with `{colors.live}`, the amber top band, or a filled amber plate.
**Do** carry every strategy state as a stamped word. Pair colour with PASSED, VOID, PAPER or LIVE so the state survives in greyscale.
**Do** show the service plate (PAPER outline or LIVE amber fill) on any board that displays money.
**Do** set figures, labels and commands in Barlow Condensed uppercase, and sentences in Barlow sentence case. Keep `tabular-nums lining-nums` on.
**Do** give every new strategy-like object the slip anatomy: serial, title, plain thesis, dashed figure row, stamp.
**Do** use the slip-rest shadow for things that sit on the counter, and recess anything placed on the board.
**Do** keep tap targets at least 44px tall, and keep input text at 16px.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion`; the global block collapses every animation and transition.
donts: **Don't** build the dark neon trading terminal or the white brokerage card grid. The counter is cool grey, slips are thermal white, and the only dark field is the green board.
**Don't** use a monospace face for labels, tickers, serials or axes.
**Don't** perforate panels, rows or forms. Tear edges belong to slips.
**Don't** add a second board band, a second ticket button, or amber text on the counter.
**Don't** let paper and live converge. LIVE is always the filled amber plate, stamp or band. PAPER is always the outline or grey stamp.
**Don't** add a third type family or an icon font. Icons are inline 1.8-stroke SVG in `currentColor`.
**Don't** add a build step or framework. The surface is vanilla HTML, CSS and JS served from `app/static/`.
